clause_analysis.title: Probationary Period
clause_analysis.original_clause: 2. PROBATIONARY PERIOD The probationary period will be of ___________ and the company will evaluate the new hire’s qualifications, skills and "fit" within our Company. The given time frame does not constitute an obligation on the part of the Company to retain the employee until the end of the probationary period. This period involves special orientation activities plus closer and more frequent performance evaluations than that given to regular employees. During this time or at any time of employment, the Company may terminate the working relationship without cause with advance notice, except as prescribed by law. At the end of the probationary period, if the employee has not been available to work the full probationary period or work performance has not met expectations, the length of the probation may be extended by the Company at its sole discretion. Upon satisfactory completion of the probationary period, the employee will achieve a regular or part time employee status and as such, will be eligible for most of our benefits (exceptions would be benefits that have a specific waiting period). The employee will now be expected to meet and maintain Company standards for job performance and behavior.
clause_analysis.reason: The unilateral modification clause may be considered unfair to the employee, as it allows the company to extend the probationary period at its sole discretion without providing the employee with adequate notice or an opportunity to improve.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Request the company to revise the clause to provide the employee with a minimum of thirty (30) days' prior written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure any performance issues before extending the probationary period.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of fairness and transparency in the employment contract, and suggest that the company consider providing the employee with regular performance feedback and a clear understanding of the expectations during the probationary period.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: The probationary period will be of six (6) months. The company will evaluate the new hire's qualifications, skills, and 'fit' within our Company. The given time frame does not constitute an obligation on the part of the Company to retain the employee until the end of the probationary period. This period involves special orientation activities plus closer and more frequent performance evaluations than that given to regular employees. During this time or at any time of employment, the Company may terminate the working relationship without cause with advance notice of at least thirty (30) days, except as prescribed by law. At the end of the probationary period, if the employee has not been available to work the full probationary period or work performance has not met expectations, the Company will provide the employee with written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure any performance issues before extending the probationary period. Upon satisfactory completion of the probationary period, the employee will achieve a regular or part-time employee status and as such, will be eligible for most of our benefits (exceptions would be benefits that have a specific waiting period). The employee will now be expected to meet and maintain Company standards for job performance and behavior.

clause_analysis.title: Liability
clause_analysis.original_clause: 4.6 As ______________of the Company the Employee shall be responsible for the day-to-day management to immediate Head or Senior in hierarchy.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause lacks clarity on the Employee's responsibilities and may lead to disputes regarding day-to-day management.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Revise the clause to clearly define the Employee's responsibilities and the process for escalating issues to the Head or Senior in hierarchy.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider adding a provision for regular check-ins between the Employee and their Head or Senior in hierarchy to ensure that issues are addressed promptly and effectively.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 4.6 As part of the Company, the Employee shall be responsible for the day-to-day management of their assigned tasks and shall report any issues or concerns to their immediate Head or Senior in hierarchy, who shall provide guidance and support as necessary.

clause_analysis.title: Amendment
clause_analysis.original_clause: 4.7 That the employee services will be governed by the rules and regulations of the company as in force from time to time and also as per certified model. The Employer can modify the Agreement or Rules and Regulations from time to time and the modification will be applicable from the same day.
clause_analysis.reason: The unilateral modification clause may be overly broad and could potentially allow the Employer to make significant changes to the Agreement without adequate notice or input from the Employee.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a revised clause that requires prior written notice and mutual consent for any material changes to the Agreement.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider adding a provision that allows the Employee to opt-out of any changes that are not mutually agreed upon, and ensure that the revised clause is clear and specific about what constitutes a material change.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 4.7 The parties agree to review and update the Agreement as necessary, and any changes shall be made in writing and signed by both parties. The Employer shall provide the Employee with prior written notice of any proposed changes, and the Employee shall have the right to opt-out of any changes that are not mutually agreed upon.

clause_analysis.title: Salary
clause_analysis.original_clause: 5.2 The Employee shall not entitle to get salary, if he/she fails to meet the objectives or targets laid down by the company.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may be considered unfair as it allows the company to withhold salary without providing a clear opportunity for the employee to meet the objectives or targets.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Review and revise the clause to provide a clear opportunity for the employee to meet the objectives or targets, and to specify the consequences of failure to meet these objectives.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider negotiating a clause that provides a clear process for the employee to meet the objectives or targets, and specifies the consequences of failure to meet these objectives, while also ensuring that the employee has a reasonable opportunity to rectify the situation.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 5.2 The Employee shall be entitled to receive salary as per the company's payment schedule, subject to meeting the objectives or targets laid down by the company. In the event of failure to meet these objectives, the Employee shall be given a reasonable opportunity to rectify the situation within a specified timeframe, and the company shall provide written notice of any intended action.

clause_analysis.title: Intellectual Property
clause_analysis.original_clause: 6.2 As long as the Employee is employed, and also thereafter, he/she shall maintain confidential the corporate secrets and all other information of a confidential nature pertaining to the Company and its operations. The Employee may use such information only during his/her employment by the Company and in the interest of the Company. The Employee shall at all times carefully and diligently safeguard and promote the Company’s interests.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may be overly broad and restrictive, potentially infringing on the employee's rights and limiting their ability to work in the same industry after employment.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Consider revising the clause to limit the restrictions on the employee's post-employment activities, such as by specifying a reasonable time period, geographic scope, and scope of prohibited activities.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate for a more balanced clause that protects the Company's interests while also allowing the Employee to work in the same industry after employment, provided they do not disclose confidential information or solicit existing clients.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 6.2 The Employee shall maintain confidentiality of corporate secrets and information of a confidential nature pertaining to the Company and its operations during employment and for a period of three (3) years thereafter. The Employee may use such information only during employment by the Company and in the interest of the Company. The Employee shall at all times carefully and diligently safeguard and promote the Company’s interests.

clause_analysis.title: Intellectual Property
clause_analysis.original_clause: 6.3 During the course of employment, any such creation, innovation or any such intellectual property in the form of software, hardware etc shall be exclusive property of the company as well the source code of the company shall remain exclusive property of the company. That the employee shall not use the source code of the company directly or indirectly. If the company finds that the employee is contravening this term directly or indirectly then the company shall be entitled to claim damages under section 73, 74 of the contract act and also entitled to initiate legal proceeding against the employee.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause overbroadly assigns exclusive ownership of all intellectual property created by the employee during employment, including source code, without any limitations or exceptions.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a revised clause that limits the company's ownership to intellectual property created using company resources or relating to company business, and excludes personal projects or ideas developed outside of work hours.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of preserving the employee's personal intellectual property rights and creative freedom outside of work hours, while ensuring the company's legitimate interests in protecting its business assets and confidential information.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 6.3 During the course of employment, any such creation, innovation, or intellectual property in the form of software, hardware, etc., created using company resources or relating to company business, shall be the exclusive property of the company. The employee shall not use the source code of the company directly or indirectly without prior written permission from the company. If the company finds that the employee is contravening this term, it shall provide written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure before initiating any legal proceedings.

clause_analysis.title: Non-Compete
clause_analysis.original_clause: 7.1 That the employee after the period of employment is over, shall not open similar nature company upto three years directly or indirectly. If the company finds that the employee is contravening this term directly or indirectly, then the company shall be entitled to claim damages under section 73,
clause_analysis.reason: The original non-compete clause is overbroad as it restricts the employee from opening a similar nature company for three years directly or indirectly, which may be too restrictive and limit the employee's future opportunities.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a revised non-compete clause that limits restrictions by time, geography, and scope, and consider replacing it with a non-solicitation/confidentiality protection clause.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of preserving the employee's future opportunities and flexibility, while still protecting the company's legitimate business interests.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 7.1 The employee shall not, for a period of one year after leaving employment, solicit or induce any customer or client of the company to become a customer or client of a competing business. The employee shall also protect the confidentiality of the company's confidential information and trade secrets.

clause_analysis.title: Non-Compete
clause_analysis.original_clause: 74 of the contract act as well as entitled to initiate appropriate legal proceeding against the employee. 7.2 That the client or the customer shall be sole client of the company. During the employment period as well as after the employment period is over, if the company finds out that the employee is trying to connect with the client of the company directly or indirectly, then the company shall be entitled to claim damages under section 73, 74 of the contract act as well as entitled to initiate appropriate legal proceeding against the employee.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause imposes an overly broad and vague penalty on the employee for attempting to connect with the company's clients, which may be considered an unreasonable restraint of trade and may not be enforceable under Indian contract law.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Revisit the clause to ensure it is reasonable, necessary, and proportionate to the legitimate business interests of the company, and consider limiting the penalty to reasonable, documented, and legally recoverable actual costs.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider negotiating a more balanced clause that protects the company's legitimate business interests while also providing the employee with reasonable protection and recourse, and ensure that the clause is clear, objective, and enforceable under Indian contract law.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: During the employment period as well as after the employment period is over, if the company finds out that the employee is trying to connect with the company's clients directly or indirectly, the company shall be entitled to claim damages under section 73, 74 of the contract act, limited to reasonable, documented, and legally recoverable actual costs, and shall provide the employee with prior written notice and a reasonable opportunity to respond.

clause_analysis.title: Salary
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.2 The Employee may lawfully terminate this Employment Agreement by giving to the Employer not less than notice in writing and the employee shall not be entitled to get the salary of the notice period and on break of bond of two years the employee is liable to pay penalty equal to Rs. 2 lakhs. Employer can terminate the employee any time with immediate effect without giving any Notice Period.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause imposes an unfair penalty on the employee for terminating the employment agreement without notice, which may be in violation of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a revised clause that limits the penalty to reasonable, documented actual costs, with prior written notice and an opportunity to respond.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of fairness and reasonableness in the penalty clause, and suggest using a standard industry practice or a formula-based approach to determine the penalty, rather than a fixed amount.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.2 The Employee may lawfully terminate this Employment Agreement by giving to the Employer not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice. In the event of termination without notice, the Employee shall be entitled to receive accrued salary, benefits, and dues. The Employer may terminate the Employee's services with prior written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure any deficiencies. The Employee shall not be liable for any penalty or damages unless proven gross misconduct.

clause_analysis.title: Penalty
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.3 In case if the employee leaves the company or terminates his/her employment before completion of two years, then he/she is liable to pay penalty equal to Rs. 2 lakhs. Since the Employer’s company is a software developing company as well as a reputed Training Academy that enjoys tremendous goodwill in the market. Since, a lot of time, energy and effort is devoted and invested in grooming young aspiring Employees which is essential in bringing out the best of talent in them and nurturing them to make them able, competent and successful professionals.
clause_analysis.reason: The penalty clause is excessive and may be considered unfair to the employee, as it does not provide any reasonable opportunity to cure or mitigate the damages.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate with the employer to reduce the penalty amount or provide a reasonable opportunity to cure, and consider including a clause that limits recovery to actual costs incurred by the employer.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of fairness and reasonableness in the penalty clause, and suggest that the employer consider providing a more nuanced approach to addressing potential damages, such as a sliding scale of penalties based on the employee's length of service or a requirement for the employer to provide evidence of actual costs incurred.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.3 In case of termination of employment before completion of two years, the employee shall be liable to pay a penalty equal to the actual costs incurred by the employer in recruiting, training, and onboarding the employee, as documented and provided to the employee in writing prior to termination. The employer shall provide the employee with thirty (30) days prior written notice of termination and a reasonable opportunity to cure any deficiencies.

clause_analysis.title: Liability
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.6 That if the employee commits any offence punishable under the Indian Law even outside the company or with the customer outside the course of employment, the company shall not be responsible for it in any circumstances.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may lead to unforeseen consequences for the company due to its absolute liability for the employee's actions outside the scope of employment.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Review and revise the clause to limit the company's liability to reasonable, documented actual costs, with prior written notice and an opportunity to respond.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider negotiating a reasonable liability cap and a clear process for determining liability, to ensure that the company's exposure is limited and predictable.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.6 That if the employee commits any offence punishable under the Indian Law even outside the company or with the customer outside the course of employment, the company shall only be liable for reasonable, documented actual costs incurred by the company, and such liability shall be subject to prior written notice and an opportunity to respond.

clause_analysis.title: Liability
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.7 That during the course of employment, if the employee commits any fraud with the company and as a result of which the company suffers huge loss, in case of such an event, the Employer shall be entitled to recover the same from the employee’s movable and immovable property by instituting legal / court proceedings.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause imposes unlimited liability on the employee for fraud, which may be considered excessive and may deter employees from reporting genuine issues.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a reasonable liability cap, such as a maximum amount or a percentage of the company's loss, to balance the interests of both parties.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider proposing a cap on liability that is proportional to the employee's role and responsibilities, and ensure that the cap is clearly defined and communicated to the employee.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.7 In the event of any fraud committed by the employee during the course of employment, resulting in a loss to the company, the Employer shall be entitled to recover a maximum of 50% of the actual loss from the employee's movable and immovable property, subject to prior written notice and an opportunity for the employee to respond.

clause_analysis.title: Termination
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9 Notwithstanding the above, Employment Agreement can be terminated on the following grounds:
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may be considered unfair as it allows termination without notice for unsatisfactory performance, which could be subjective and may not provide the employee with sufficient opportunity to improve.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Consider revising the clause to include a reasonable notice period, such as thirty (30) days, and a clear opportunity for the employee to cure any unsatisfactory performance.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate for a more balanced clause that protects both the employer's interests and the employee's rights, and ensure that any termination grounds are clearly defined and objective.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9 Notwithstanding the above, Employment Agreement can be terminated on the following grounds: (i) proven gross misconduct; or (ii) unsatisfactory performance, provided the employee is given thirty (30) days prior written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure any performance issues, and written reasons for termination are given to the employee.

clause_analysis.title: Termination
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.1 Employee being found guilty of any dishonesty, misconduct, willful neglect of duty or other conduct amounting to gross misconduct with fellow colleagues or seniors;
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may be considered overly broad and potentially unfair, as it does not specify the grounds for termination or provide adequate notice to the employee.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Consider revising the clause to include specific grounds for termination, provide a reasonable notice period, and ensure compliance with applicable employment laws.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate for a more balanced clause that protects both the employer's interests and the employee's rights, and consider including a provision for a reasonable opportunity to cure any misconduct.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.1 In the event of proven gross misconduct, the employer may terminate the employment relationship with thirty (30) days prior written notice, providing written reasons for termination. The employee shall be entitled to payment of accrued salary, benefits, and dues. The employer shall also provide a reasonable opportunity to cure any misconduct prior to termination.

clause_analysis.title: Breach
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.2 Employee committing a material breach of the terms and conditions of this Employment Agreement;
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may be considered overly broad and potentially unfair to the employee, as it allows termination for a 'material breach' without specifying what constitutes a material breach or providing adequate notice and opportunity to cure.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Consider revising the clause to provide a clear definition of 'material breach' and include a reasonable notice period and opportunity to cure before termination.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate for a more specific and fair definition of 'material breach' that aligns with industry standards and best practices, and ensure that the notice period and opportunity to cure are reasonable and adequate.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.2 The employee shall be deemed to have committed a material breach of this Employment Agreement if they fail to comply with any term or condition of this Agreement, provided that such failure is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from the employer specifying the breach and the opportunity to cure.

clause_analysis.title: Employee being found to be medically unfit or,
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.3 Employee being found to be medically unfit or,
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may be considered unfair as it allows termination without specifying grounds, which could lead to arbitrary dismissal.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Consider revising the clause to include specific and objective termination grounds, such as performance issues or misconduct, to ensure fairness and protect employee rights.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate for a more balanced clause that includes a clear definition of termination grounds, a reasonable notice period, and an opportunity for the employee to cure any issues before termination.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.3 The company may terminate this Agreement only on grounds of proven gross misconduct or unsatisfactory performance, as determined by a fair and impartial process, with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice to the employee, and an opportunity to cure any issues before termination.

clause_analysis.title: Employee being declared a bankrupt or insolvent or,
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.4 Employee being declared a bankrupt or insolvent or,
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may unfairly terminate the employee's contract without providing sufficient grounds or notice.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Review and revise the termination clause to include fair and reasonable grounds for termination, such as gross misconduct, and provide a minimum of thirty (30) days prior written notice.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate for a more balanced termination clause that protects both the employee's rights and the employer's interests, and consider including a cure period and a requirement for written reasons for termination.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.4 Employee being declared a bankrupt or insolvent or, upon thirty (30) days prior written notice, for gross misconduct proven by the employer, provided that the employee is given a reasonable opportunity to cure any deficiency and is paid all accrued salary, benefits, and dues.

clause_analysis.title: Termination
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.5 Employee being convicted of any offence involving moral turpitude or defined under the Indian Law,
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may unfairly terminate an employee's contract based on a conviction of any offence involving moral turpitude or defined under the Indian Law, without providing adequate safeguards or due process.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Review and revise the termination grounds to ensure they are fair, reasonable, and compliant with applicable employment laws and regulations.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate with the other party to include a clear and objective standard for determining what constitutes 'moral turpitude' or an offence under the Indian Law, and ensure that the termination process is fair, reasonable, and compliant with applicable employment laws and regulations.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.5 Employee being convicted of any offence involving moral turpitude or defined under the Indian Law, shall be subject to a thorough investigation and review by the company. The company shall provide the employee with prior written notice and a reasonable opportunity to respond before taking any disciplinary action. The employee's termination shall be in accordance with applicable employment laws and regulations, and the company shall ensure that the termination is fair and reasonable.

clause_analysis.title: Termination
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.6 Misappropriation of the Company’s monies or property by the Employee or;
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause may be considered overly broad and potentially unfair to the Employee, as it does not specify the circumstances under which the Company may terminate the Employee's employment.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Consider revising the clause to include specific grounds for termination, such as gross misconduct or failure to meet performance expectations, and provide the Employee with a reasonable opportunity to cure any deficiencies.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate for a more balanced clause that protects both the Company's interests and the Employee's rights, and consider including a provision for prior written notice and a reasonable cure period.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.6 In the event of gross misconduct or failure to meet performance expectations, the Company may terminate the Employee's employment with prior written notice of at least thirty (30) days, providing the Employee with a reasonable opportunity to cure any deficiencies. The Company shall pay the Employee all accrued salary, benefits, and dues upon termination.

clause_analysis.title: Misconduct or insubordination on the part of the Employee,
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.7 Misconduct or insubordination on the part of the Employee,
clause_analysis.reason: Immediate dismissal without notice may be considered unfair and potentially in breach of applicable employment laws, which require a reasonable notice period or grounds for termination.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Review and revise the termination clause to include a minimum thirty (30) days prior written notice, a reasonable opportunity to cure, and written reasons for termination, except in cases of proven gross misconduct.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Consider negotiating for a more balanced termination clause that protects both the employer's interests and the employee's rights, and ensure that the clause is compliant with applicable employment laws and regulations.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.7 Termination for cause shall require at least thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Employee, stating the grounds of termination in writing, except where immediate termination is required due to proven gross misconduct. The Employee shall be given a reasonable opportunity to cure any alleged misconduct or insubordination before termination. The Employer shall pay the Employee all accrued salary, benefits, and dues upon termination.

clause_analysis.title: Rights
clause_analysis.issue_identified: Termination or suspension without reasonable notice
clause_analysis.original_clause: 8.9.8 Infringement of any Company rules and regulations by the Employee. The Employee shall be liable to be dismissed or discharged forthwith notwithstanding the rights and without giving any notice, which the Company may otherwise have against the Employee in case of any loss (grave or remote) caused by the employee during the course of his/her employment and the losses will be borne by him/her by way of damages which shall be calculated by the management of the company.
clause_analysis.reason: The original clause imposes an overly broad and draconian penalty on the Employee for infringement of Company rules and regulations, potentially allowing for termination without notice and without giving the Employee an opportunity to cure or respond.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a revised clause that provides for a reasonable notice period, an opportunity for the Employee to cure any infringement, and limits the Company's ability to terminate the Employee without just cause.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of providing the Employee with a fair opportunity to correct any mistakes or infractions, and ensure that the Company's termination rights are not overly broad or arbitrary.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 8.9.8 Infringement of any Company rules and regulations by the Employee. The Employee shall be liable for any losses caused by such infringement. The Company shall provide the Employee with written notice of the infringement and a reasonable opportunity to cure within thirty (30) days. If the Employee fails to cure, the Company may terminate the Employee's employment, but only after providing thirty (30) days' prior written notice and paying the Employee all accrued salary, benefits, and dues. The losses shall be borne by the Employee by way of damages, which shall be calculated by the management of the company and shall not exceed the actual costs incurred by the Company.

clause_analysis.title: Modification

clause_analysis.reason: The unilateral modification clause may be overly restrictive and may not account for unforeseen circumstances, potentially leading to disputes and legal issues.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Consider revising the clause to allow for mutual written consent or prior written notice for any modifications to the employment agreement.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Negotiate a compromise that balances the need for flexibility with the need for clarity and protection for both parties, and consider including a clear dispute resolution process to address any potential issues that may arise.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: 10.1 This Employment Agreement contains a complete statement of all the arrangements between the Company and the Employee with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all previous agreements, written or oral relating to the subject matter of this Employment Agreement. Any modifications to this Agreement shall be made in writing and signed by both parties, or by prior written notice to the other party with a reasonable opportunity to respond and cure any issues.
